name: B10-0232/2024 (S&D) – 11th year of the occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol by the Russian Federation and the deteriorating human rights situation in occupied Crimea, notably the cases of Iryna Danylovych, Tofik Abdul
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the 11th year of the occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol by the Russian Federation and the deteriorating human rights situation in occupied Crimea, notably the cases of Iryna Danylovych, Tofik Abdulhaziiev and Amet Suleymanov
part_text:
The European Parliament restates that Russia's occupation of Crimea is illegal and that Crimea belongs to Ukraine. It asks Russia to free jailed human rights defenders and political prisoners, including several who are seriously ill, and to let journalists and monitors into Crimea. It wants the Crimean Tatar assembly, the Mejlis, restored within Ukraine's system, and new European Union sanctions on officials who persecute activists. This is a statement of the Parliament's position; it does not itself change any law.

- Nothing changes yet: the Parliament is stating demands, not passing law.
- Russia, jailed activists and their families, and named officials are affected.
- The resolution goes to European Union governments and Russia; sanctions depend on them.
